l18.how: Percent means out of 100. 0.36 is 36 hundredths, so it is 36%.
Multiply the top and bottom by 4 to get 28/100. 28 out of 100 is 28%.

l18.q: Write 60% as a fraction in simplest form.
l18.how: 60% is 60/100. Divide the top and bottom by 20 to get 3/5.
0.6 is the same as 0.60, which is 60 hundredths, so it is 60%. Be careful: 6% would be 0.06.
Change each one to a percent. 0.7 is 70%, 3/4 is 75%, and 65% stays 65%. 75% is the greatest, so 3/4 wins.
Multiply by 100: 1.25 × 100 = 125%. A percent over 100% means more than one whole.

l18.q: 18 of the 50 passengers chose a window seat. What percent is that?
l18.how: Multiply the top and bottom of 18/50 by 2 to get 36/100, which is 36%.

l19.how: 10% of 260 is 26. 5% is half of 10%, so it is 26 ÷ 2 = 13.
25% of 48 is 48 ÷ 4 = 12. 75% is three of those: 12 × 3 = 36.

l19.q: A plane has 180 seats. 30% of them are premium seats. How many premium seats are there?
l19.how: 10% of 180 is 18. 30% is 3 times that: 18 × 3 = 54. (126 is the other 70%.)
100% of 40 is 40 and 50% is 20. Add them: 40 + 20 = 60. More than 100% gives more than the whole.

l19.q: A pilot has flown 20% of a 1,350-mile trip. How many miles has she flown?
l19.how: 10% of 1,350 is 135. 20% is twice that: 135 × 2 = 270. (1,080 is the 80% still to fly.)

l19.q: Which is the same as finding 50% of a number?
l19.how: 50% means 50 out of 100, which is one half. Taking half of a number is the same as dividing it by 2.

l20.q: 12 is 20% of a number. What is the number?
l20.how: 20% is one fifth, so the whole is 5 times the part: 12 × 5 = 60. Check: 20% of 60 is 12.
50% is half, so the whole is twice the part: 45 × 2 = 90.

l20.q: 18 seats are 10% of the seats on a plane. How many seats are on the plane?
l20.how: 10% is one tenth, so the whole is 10 times the part: 18 × 10 = 180.

l20.q: 33 is 75% of a number. What is the number?
l20.how: 75% is three fourths. 33 ÷ 3 = 11 is one fourth, so the whole is 11 × 4 = 44. (24.75 is 75% of 33, which answers a different question.)

l20.q: A pilot has finished 40% of her training hours. She has done 26 hours. How many hours is the whole training?
l20.how: Whole = part ÷ percent = 26 ÷ 0.40 = 65. Check: 40% of 65 is 26.

l20.q: 9 is 3% of a number. What is the number?
l20.how: If 3% is 9, then 1% is 9 ÷ 3 = 3. The whole is 100%, so 3 × 100 = 300.

l20.q: A sale took $14 off the price, and that was 35% off. What was the original price?
l20.how: Whole = part ÷ percent = 14 ÷ 0.35 = 40. Check: 35% of $40 is $14.

l20.q: 15 is 60% of a number. Which calculation finds the number?
l20.how: Part = percent × whole, so whole = part ÷ percent. 15 ÷ 0.60 = 25, and 60% of 25 is 15.

l21.q: An $80 headset is 15% off. What is the sale price?
l21.how: 15% of 80 is 0.15 × 80 = 12. That is the discount. Sale price = 80 − 12 = $68.

l21.q: A meal costs $40. You leave a 20% tip. What is the total?
l21.how: 20% of 40 is 8. Add the tip to the meal: 40 + 8 = $48.

l21.q: A pilot earned $2,000 a month and got a 5% raise. What is the new monthly pay?
A cap's price went up from $50 to $60. By what percent did it go up?
l21.how: It went up $10. Compare the change to the original price: 10 out of 50 is 20%. (About 16.7% compares to the new price by mistake.)

l21.q: A cadet got 22 out of 25 questions right. What percent is that?
l21.how: Multiply the top and bottom of 22/25 by 4 to get 88/100, which is 88%.

l21.q: A $120 ticket has an 8% tax added. How much is the tax?
l21.how: 8% is 0.08. 0.08 × 120 = 9.6, so the tax is $9.60. ($129.60 is the total, not the tax.)

l21.q: A $30 cap is 25% off. How much money do you save?
l21.how: 25% is one fourth. 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5, so you save $7.50. ($22.50 is what you pay.)

l21.q: An airline had 400 flights last week. 92% left on time. How many flights left late?
l21.how: 100% − 92% = 8% were late. 1% of 400 is 4, so 8% is 8 × 4 = 32. (368 flights were on time.)

n6.q: Which is the best estimate of 49% of 812?
n6.how: 49% is close to 50%, which is half. 812 is close to 800. Half of 800 is 400.

n6.q: Which is the best estimate of 9% of 610?
n6.how: 9% is close to 10%, and 610 is close to 600. 10% of 600 is 60.

n6.q: Is 26% of 80 more or less than 20?
n6.how: 25% of 80 is one fourth, which is 20. 26% is a bit more than 25%, so the answer is a bit more than 20. (It is 20.8.)

n6.q: A sign says "Over 70% off!" A $50 jacket now costs $20. Is the sign right about this jacket?
n6.how: The discount is 50 − 20 = $30. 30 out of 50 is 60%, which is less than 70%. (40% is the part you still pay.)

n6.q: Which is the best estimate of 74% of 201?
n6.how: 74% is close to 75%, and 201 is close to 200. 75% of 200 is three fourths of 200, which is 150.

n6.q: Which is larger: 10% of 500 or 50% of 90?
n6.how: 10% of 500 is 50. 50% of 90 is half of 90, which is 45. 50 is larger than 45.

n6.q: A cadet estimated 33% of 90 as about 60. Which statement is correct?
n6.a: The estimate is too high. 33% is about one third, so the answer is about 30.
choices: The estimate is too high. 33% is about one third, so the answer is about 30.
The estimate is too low. The answer is about 90.
The estimate is too high. The answer is about 3.
n6.how: 33% is very close to one third. One third of 90 is 30, so 60 is about twice too big.

m6a.q: In the expression 9 + 4k, what is the constant?
m6a.how: The constant is the number with no variable. 4 is the coefficient of k, and 9 stands alone, so 9 is the constant.

m6a.q: Which expression means "a number n increased by 6"?
m6a.how: "Increased by" means add. Start with n and add 6: n + 6.

m6a.q: Which expression means "5 times a number x"?
m6a.how: "Times" means multiply. 5 times x is written 5x, with the number in front of the variable.
Put 4 in for a: 3 × 4 + 2. Multiply first: 12 + 2 = 14. (18 adds before multiplying.)

m6a.q: Which expression means "the quotient of a number y and 8"?
m6a.how: Quotient means divide, in the order the words give: y divided by 8 is y ÷ 8.

m6a.q: A taxi charges $3 plus $2 for each mile, m. Which expression shows the cost in dollars?
m6a.how: The $3 is charged once. The $2 is charged for every mile, which is 2m. Together: 3 + 2m.
Put 7 in for b: 20 − 2 × 7. Multiply first: 20 − 14 = 6.

m6a.q: How many terms are in 4x − 7 + y?
m6a.how: Terms are separated by + or − signs. The terms are 4x, 7, and y, so there are 3 terms.

m6b.how: All three are like terms. Work with the coefficients: 5 + 3 − 2 = 6, so the answer is 6w.
Combine the k terms: 2k + 5k = 7k. Combine the constants: 4 + 3 = 7. The answer is 7k + 7.
3(2m) means 3 times 2 times m. Multiply the numbers: 3 × 2 = 6, so it equals 6m.

m6b.q: Which pair of expressions is equivalent?
m6b.how: y means 1y, so 4y + y = 5y. Adding like terms never makes a square, and 2y and 3 are not like terms.

m6b.q: Are 2(x + 3) and 2x + 3 equivalent? Test with x = 1.
m6b.how: 2(1 + 3) = 2 × 4 = 8, but 2 × 1 + 3 = 5. They give different values, so they are not equivalent. The 2 must multiply the 3 as well.
c means 1c. Work with the coefficients: 9 − 4 + 1 = 6, so the answer is 6c.

m6b.q: Which expression is equivalent to n + n + n?
m6b.how: Adding n three times is 3 times n, which is 3n. n^3 would mean multiplying n by itself three times.
Combine the a terms: 2a + 4a = 6a. Combine the b terms: 3b + b = 4b. a and b are not like terms, so the answer is 6a + 4b.

m6c.how: Multiply 5 by both terms: 5 × y = 5y and 5 × 2 = 10. The answer is 5y + 10.
Multiply 6 by both terms: 6 × 3 = 18 and 6 × n = 6n. Keep the minus sign: 18 − 6n.
Multiply 2 by both terms: 2 × 4x = 8x and 2 × 5 = 10. The answer is 8x + 10.

m6c.q: Factor 4x + 12 using the greatest common factor.
m6c.how: The greatest common factor of 4 and 12 is 4. 4x ÷ 4 = x and 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so 4(x + 3). 2(2x + 6) is equivalent, but 2 is not the greatest common factor.

m6c.q: Factor 15 + 10m using the greatest common factor.
m6c.how: The greatest common factor of 15 and 10 is 5. 15 ÷ 5 = 3 and 10m ÷ 5 = 2m, so 5(3 + 2m). Check by expanding: 15 + 10m.
Multiply 7 by both terms: 7 × a = 7a and 7 × 3 = 21. The answer is 7a + 21.

m6c.q: Use the distributive property to find 4 × 23 by thinking of it as 4(20 + 3).
m6c.how: 4 × 20 = 80 and 4 × 3 = 12. Add them: 80 + 12 = 92. (83 forgets to multiply the 3 by 4.)

m6c.q: Factor 18y − 24 using the greatest common factor.
m6c.how: The greatest common factor of 18 and 24 is 6. 18y ÷ 6 = 3y and 24 ÷ 6 = 4, so 6(3y − 4). The other equivalent choices use a smaller common factor.

m7a.q: Which of these is an expression?
m7a.how: An expression has no equal sign and no inequality symbol. 4x − 9 is the only one with neither.
Put 5 in for x: 3 × 5 + 2 = 15 + 2 = 17. Both sides are equal, so 5 is a solution.

m7a.q: Which value of y makes y + 8 = 20 true?
Which value is a solution of n > 7?
m7a.how: n > 7 means n is greater than 7. 9 is greater than 7. 7 itself is not greater than 7, so it does not count.

m7a.q: A plane can carry at most 150 passengers. Let p be the number of passengers. Which inequality shows this?
m7a.how: "At most 150" means 150 or fewer, so p is less than or equal to 150: p ≤ 150.

m7a.q: Which equation says "twice a number is 36"?
m7a.how: Twice a number means 2 times the number, 2n. "Is" means equals, so 2n = 36.

m7a.q: Which value of m makes m − 6 = 9 true?
Which of these is an inequality?
m7a.how: An inequality uses <, >, ≤, or ≥. Only k + 3 ≥ 11 uses one of those symbols.

m7b.q: What does the graph of x ≥ 4 look like on a number line?
m7b.a: A closed circle at 4 and an arrow pointing right
choices: A closed circle at 4 and an arrow pointing right
An open circle at 4 and an arrow pointing right
A closed circle at 4 and an arrow pointing left
An open circle at 4 and an arrow pointing left
m7b.how: ≥ includes 4, so the circle is closed (filled in). Greater than means bigger numbers, so the arrow points right.

m7b.q: You must be at least 12 years old to fly alone. Let a be the age. Which inequality shows this?
m7b.how: "At least 12" means 12 or older, so 12 is included: a ≥ 12.

m7b.q: Which number is a solution of x < −1?
m7b.how: x < −1 means numbers to the left of −1 on the number line. −3 is to the left. −1 itself is not included.

m7b.q: A suitcase must weigh less than 23 kilograms. Let w be the weight. Which inequality shows this?
m7b.how: "Less than 23" does not include 23, so use <: w < 23.

m7b.q: How many solutions does x > 6 have?
m7b.how: Every number greater than 6 works: 7, 8, 6.5, 100, and so on forever. So there are infinitely many solutions.

m7b.q: Which inequality has 2 as a solution but not 5?
m7b.how: Check both numbers. 2 < 4 is true and 5 < 4 is false, so x < 4 works. Each other choice includes 5 or leaves out 2.

m7b.q: A graph has an open circle at −2 and an arrow pointing left. Which inequality does it show?
m7b.how: An open circle means −2 is not included. Pointing left means smaller numbers. So x < −2.

m7b.q: A drone can fly no higher than 120 meters. Which height is NOT allowed?
m7b.how: "No higher than 120" means h ≤ 120. 120 is allowed because it is equal. 125 is higher than 120, so it is not allowed.

m7c.how: Undo subtracting 9 by adding 9 to both sides: y = 15 + 9 = 24. Check: 24 − 9 = 15.
7k means 7 times k. Undo multiplying by dividing both sides by 7: k = 56 ÷ 7 = 8.
Undo dividing by 4 by multiplying both sides by 4: x = 12 × 4 = 48. Check: 48 ÷ 4 = 12.
Undo adding 2.5 by subtracting 2.5 from both sides: m = 10 − 2.5 = 7.5.
Subtract 3/4 from both sides: p = 2 − 3/4. 2 is 8/4, and 8/4 − 3/4 = 5/4 = 1 1/4.

m7c.q: A plane has 38 empty seats after 112 passengers board. Which equation finds the total number of seats, s?
m7c.how: Total seats minus the seats taken leaves the empty seats: s − 112 = 38. Solving gives s = 150.

m7c.q: Five pilots share 60 snack bars equally. Solve 5b = 60 to find how many bars each pilot gets.
m7c.how: Divide both sides by 5: b = 60 ÷ 5 = 12. Each pilot gets 12 bars.
Undo subtracting 4.6 by adding 4.6 to both sides: n = 3.2 + 4.6 = 7.8.

m8a.q: Start at the origin. Move 4 units left and 3 units up. What is the ordered pair?
m8a.how: Left means a negative x, so x = −4. Up means a positive y, so y = 3. Write x first: (−4, 3).

m8a.q: In which quadrant is the point (5, −2)?
m8a.how: x is positive (right) and y is negative (down). That is (+, −), Quadrant IV, at the bottom right.

m8a.q: What are the coordinates of the origin?
m8a.how: The origin is where the x-axis and y-axis cross. You have not moved left, right, up, or down, so it is (0, 0).

m8a.q: A point is on the y-axis, 6 units below the origin. What is its ordered pair?
m8a.how: On the y-axis, x is 0. Below the origin means y is negative, so the point is (0, −6).

m8a.q: The point (3, 4) is reflected across the x-axis. What is the new point?
m8a.how: Flipping across the x-axis keeps x the same and changes the sign of y. (3, 4) becomes (3, −4).

m8a.q: Which point is in Quadrant II?
m8a.how: Quadrant II is the top left, where x is negative and y is positive. (−1, 7) is (−, +).

m8a.q: In the ordered pair (8, −5), what does the 8 tell you?
m8a.how: The first number is x, which moves left or right. 8 is positive, so move 8 units right.

m8a.q: The point (−2, −6) is reflected across the y-axis. What is the new point?
m8a.how: Flipping across the y-axis keeps y the same and changes the sign of x. (−2, −6) becomes (2, −6).

m8b.q: What is the distance between (3, 2) and (3, 9)?
m8b.how: Same x, so use the y-coordinates. 2 and 9 have the same sign, so subtract: 9 − 2 = 7 units.

m8b.q: What is the distance between (−4, −1) and (5, −1)?
m8b.how: Same y, so use the x-coordinates. −4 and 5 have opposite signs, so add the absolute values: 4 + 5 = 9 units.

m8b.q: What is the distance between (0, −7) and (0, 3)?
m8b.how: Same x, so use the y-coordinates. −7 and 3 have opposite signs, so add the absolute values: 7 + 3 = 10 units.

m8b.q: A rectangle has corners at (1, 1), (6, 1), (6, 4), and (1, 4). What is its perimeter?
m8b.how: The width is 6 − 1 = 5 and the height is 4 − 1 = 3. Perimeter = 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 units. (15 is the area.)

m8b.q: A rectangle has corners at (−2, 0), (4, 0), (4, 5), and (−2, 5). What is its area?
m8b.how: The width is |−2| + 4 = 6 and the height is 5. Area = 6 × 5 = 30 square units. (22 is the perimeter.)

m8b.q: What is the distance between (−6, 2) and (−1, 2)?
m8b.how: Same y, so use the x-coordinates. −6 and −1 have the same sign, so subtract the absolute values: 6 − 1 = 5 units.

m8b.q: A(2, −3) and B(2, 5) are the ends of one side of a square. How long is each side of the square?
m8b.how: Same x, so use the y-coordinates. −3 and 5 have opposite signs, so add: 3 + 5 = 8. A square has 4 equal sides, so each is 8 units.

m8b.q: On a map grid where each unit is 10 miles, a pilot flies straight from (−3, 4) to (−3, −2). How far is the trip?
m8b.how: Same x, so use the y-coordinates: 4 and −2 have opposite signs, so add 4 + 2 = 6 units. Each unit is 10 miles: 6 × 10 = 60 miles.

l17.q: There are 12 inches in 1 foot. How many inches are in 7 feet?
l17.how: Inches are smaller than feet, so there will be more of them. Multiply: 7 × 12 = 84.

l17.q: There are 1,000 meters in 1 kilometer. A runway is 3,500 meters long. How many kilometers is that?
l17.how: Kilometers are bigger than meters, so there will be fewer of them. Divide: 3,500 ÷ 1,000 = 3.5.

l17.q: There are 60 minutes in 1 hour. A flight lasts 150 minutes. How many hours is that?
l17.how: Divide: 150 ÷ 60 = 2.5 hours, which is 2 hours and 30 minutes. (2.3 mixes up 30 minutes with 0.3 of an hour.)

l17.q: There are 16 ounces in 1 pound. A bag weighs 48 ounces. How many pounds is that?
l17.how: Pounds are bigger than ounces, so there will be fewer of them. Divide: 48 ÷ 16 = 3 pounds.

l17.q: There are 4 quarts in 1 gallon. How many quarts are in 6.5 gallons?
l17.how: Quarts are smaller than gallons, so multiply: 6.5 × 4 = 26 quarts.

l17.q: There are 3 feet in 1 yard. A hallway is 45 feet long. How many yards is that?
l17.how: Yards are bigger than feet, so divide: 45 ÷ 3 = 15 yards.

l17.q: 1 inch is about 2.54 centimeters. About how many centimeters are in 10 inches?
l17.how: Centimeters are smaller than inches, so multiply: 10 × 2.54 = 25.4 centimeters.

l17.q: A plane flies 9 miles every minute. At that rate, how far does it fly in 1 hour?
l17.how: 1 hour is 60 minutes. Multiply the rate by the minutes: 9 × 60 = 540 miles.

m9b.q: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is its area?
m9b.how: A = 1/2 × b × h = 1/2 × 10 × 6 = 1/2 × 60 = 30 square centimeters. 60 forgets the 1/2.

m9b.q: A parallelogram has a base of 8 feet and a height of 5 feet. What is its area?
m9b.how: A = b × h = 8 × 5 = 40 square feet. A parallelogram does not use 1/2.

m9b.q: A right triangle has legs of 9 meters and 4 meters. What is its area?
m9b.how: In a right triangle, the two legs are the base and the height. A = 1/2 × 9 × 4 = 18 square meters.

m9b.q: A shape is a rectangle 12 m long and 5 m tall, with a triangle on top. The triangle has a base of 12 m and a height of 4 m. What is the total area?
m9b.how: Rectangle: 12 × 5 = 60. Triangle: 1/2 × 12 × 4 = 24. Total: 60 + 24 = 84 square meters. (108 forgets the 1/2 on the triangle.)

m9b.q: A triangle has an area of 24 square inches and a base of 8 inches. What is its height?
A square with 7 cm sides is cut along a diagonal into two equal triangles. What is the area of one triangle?
m9b.how: The square's area is 7 × 7 = 49. Each triangle is half of it: 49 ÷ 2 = 24.5 square centimeters.

m9b.q: A parallelogram and a triangle have the same base (10 units) and the same height (4 units). How do their areas compare?
m9b.a: The triangle's area is half the parallelogram's area
choices: The triangle's area is half the parallelogram's area
The triangle's area is twice the parallelogram's area
The triangle's area is 4 less than the parallelogram's area
m9b.how: Parallelogram: 10 × 4 = 40. Triangle: 1/2 × 10 × 4 = 20. A triangle is half of a parallelogram with the same base and height.

m9b.q: A wing shape is made of two triangles. Each has a base of 6 feet and a height of 3 feet. What is the total area?
m9b.how: One triangle: 1/2 × 6 × 3 = 9 square feet. Two of them: 9 × 2 = 18 square feet.

m9c.q: A box is 4 cm long, 3 cm wide, and 2 cm tall. What is its volume?
m9c.how: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cubic centimeters. 9 adds the edges, and 52 is the surface area.

m9c.q: A cube has edges of 5 inches. What is its volume?
m9c.how: V = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 cubic inches. 25 is the area of one face, and 150 is the surface area.

m9c.q: A crate is 2 1/2 feet long, 2 feet wide, and 4 feet tall. What is its volume?
A prism has a base area of 18 square meters and a height of 5 meters. What is its volume?
m9c.how: V = base area × height = 18 × 5 = 90 cubic meters.

m9c.q: A box has a volume of 60 cubic inches. It is 5 inches long and 4 inches wide. How tall is it?
m9c.how: The base area is 5 × 4 = 20. Height = volume ÷ base area = 60 ÷ 20 = 3 inches.

m9c.q: How many cubes with 1/2-inch edges fit exactly in a box that is 2 inches long, 1 inch wide, and 1 inch tall?
m9c.how: Along the length, 4 half-inch cubes fit. Along the width, 2 fit, and along the height, 2 fit. 4 × 2 × 2 = 16 cubes.

m9c.q: A fuel tank is shaped like a rectangular prism, 1.5 m by 2 m by 3 m. What is its volume?
You double the height of a box but keep its length and width the same. What happens to the volume?
m9c.how: V = l × w × h. Doubling one factor doubles the product, so the volume doubles. Think of stacking a second, identical layer on top.

m9d.q: How many faces does a rectangular prism have?
m9d.how: A box has a top and a bottom, a front and a back, and a left and a right side. That is 6 faces.

m9d.q: A cube has edges of 3 cm. What is its surface area?
m9d.how: Each face is 3 × 3 = 9 square centimeters. A cube has 6 faces: 6 × 9 = 54 square centimeters. (27 is the volume.)

m9d.q: A box is 5 inches by 2 inches by 1 inch. What is its surface area?
m9d.how: The faces are 5 by 2 (10), 5 by 1 (5), and 2 by 1 (2), and each comes in a pair. 2 × (10 + 5 + 2) = 34 square inches. 17 forgets the pairs, and 10 is the volume.

m9d.q: A net has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. Which figure does it fold into?
m9d.how: The 2 triangles are the ends, and the 3 rectangles wrap around the sides. That makes a triangular prism.

m9d.q: A net is made of 6 squares that are all the same size. Which figure does it fold into?
choices: Rectangular prism with no square faces
m9d.how: A cube has 6 faces, and every face is the same square.

m9d.q: A square pyramid has a square base 4 m on each side. Each triangle face has a base of 4 m and a height of 5 m. What is its surface area?
m9d.how: Base: 4 × 4 = 16. Each triangle: 1/2 × 4 × 5 = 10, and there are 4 of them: 40. Total: 16 + 40 = 56 square meters. (96 forgets the 1/2.)

m9d.q: Why do you use surface area, not volume, to find how much paint covers a box?
m9d.a: Paint covers the outside faces, and that is an area
choices: Paint covers the outside faces, and that is an area
Paint fills up the inside of the box
Volume is always smaller than surface area
Surface area and volume are always the same number
m9d.how: Paint goes on the faces, which are flat surfaces. Volume measures the space inside, which paint does not fill.

m9d.q: A cube has a surface area of 96 square inches. What is the area of one face?
m9d.how: A cube has 6 equal faces. 96 ÷ 6 = 16 square inches per face. (24 divides by 4 by mistake.)

m10a.a: How many hours of sleep do the students in our class get on school nights?
choices: How many hours of sleep do the students in our class get on school nights?
How many hours did I sleep last night?
How many students are in our class?
m10a.how: Different students sleep different amounts, so the answers vary. Each of the others has just one answer.

m10a.q: Which is NOT a statistical question?
m10a.a: How tall is the control tower at this airport?
choices: How tall is the control tower at this airport?
How tall are the players on the basketball team?
How many pets do the families on our street have?
How many minutes late were this month's flights?
m10a.how: One tower has one height, so there is only one answer. The others ask about a group with answers that vary.

m10a.q: Why is "How old are the students in Grade 6?" a statistical question?
m10a.a: The answers vary from student to student
choices: The answers vary from student to student
m10a.how: A statistical question expects answers that vary. Students in Grade 6 are not all the same age to the month.

m10a.q: Which question would you answer by collecting data from many flights?
m10a.a: How full are Skyline Air's evening flights?
choices: How full are Skyline Air's evening flights?
What is the flight number of the 6 p.m. flight?
What city does Flight 22 fly to?
Who is the captain of tonight's flight?
m10a.how: Each evening flight has a different number of passengers, so you need data from many flights. The others each have one answer.

m10a.q: "What is my favorite color?" is not a statistical question. Which change makes it statistical?
m10a.a: What are the favorite colors of the students in my class?
choices: What are the favorite colors of the students in my class?
What is my teacher's favorite color?
m10a.how: Asking many students gives answers that vary, so it becomes a statistical question. The others still ask about just one person or thing.

m10a.a: How many minutes do students spend on homework each night?
choices: How many minutes do students spend on homework each night?
How many minutes did I spend on homework tonight?
How many minutes are in an hour?
m10a.how: Different students and different nights give different answers, so the data vary. The others have one answer.

m10a.q: Which data would answer "How far do the paper airplanes made by our class fly?"
m10a.a: The flight distance of each classmate's airplane
choices: The flight distance of each classmate's airplane
The distance of the longest paper airplane flight in the world
The length of one paper airplane
The number of students in the class
m10a.how: The question is about our class's airplanes, so you need one distance for each airplane. That gives a set of data that varies.

m10a.q: Which is NOT a statistical question?
m10a.a: How many moons does Mars have?
choices: How many moons does Mars have?
How many books did each student read this term?
What were the daily high temperatures in July?
How many emails do teachers get each day?
m10a.how: Mars has one number of moons, so there is only one answer. The others collect many values that vary.

m10b.q: The data are 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5. On a dot plot, how many dots go above 4?
m10b.how: Each value gets one dot. 4 appears three times in the list, so there are 3 dots above 4.

m10b.q: A frequency table shows the delays at a small airport: 0 delays on 5 days, 1 delay on 8 days, 2 delays on 4 days, and 3 delays on 3 days. How many days are in the data?
m10b.how: Add the frequencies (the numbers of days): 5 + 8 + 4 + 3 = 20 days. (6 adds the delay numbers instead.)

m10b.q: Use the same table: 0 delays on 5 days, 1 delay on 8 days, 2 delays on 4 days, and 3 delays on 3 days. On how many days was there at least 1 delay?
m10b.how: "At least 1" means 1, 2, or 3 delays. Add those days: 8 + 4 + 3 = 15.

m10b.q: A histogram groups ages into the intervals 10–19, 20–29, and 30–39. In which interval does the age 29 go?
choices: It does not fit any interval
m10b.how: 29 is between 20 and 29, including 29, so it goes in the 20–29 bar.

m10b.q: Which display shows each data value as its own dot above a number line?
m10b.how: A dot plot puts one dot above the number line for every value. A histogram uses bars for intervals, and a box plot shows quartiles.

m10b.q: Bags weighed 18, 21, 22, 19, 23, 21, and 20 kilograms. How many bags weighed more than 20 kilograms?
m10b.how: The weights over 20 are 21, 22, 23, and 21. Count both 21s: that is 4 bags. 20 itself is not more than 20.

m10b.q: Which display is best for showing how many values fall in equal intervals, such as 0–9 and 10–19?
m10b.how: A histogram has one bar for each interval, and the height shows how many values are in it.

m10b.q: Test scores are 70, 85, 90, 85, 95, and 80. When they are put in order from least to greatest, which value is in the 3rd position?
m10b.how: In order: 70, 80, 85, 85, 90, 95. The 3rd value is 85. (90 is 3rd in the list before ordering.)

m10c.how: Put them in order first: 3, 4, 5, 7, 9. The middle value is 5. (4 is the middle before ordering.)
The mode is the value that appears most often. 5 appears three times, more than any other value.
There are 4 values, so there are two middle values, 14 and 18. The median is halfway between them: (14 + 18) ÷ 2 = 16. (15.5 is the mean.)

m10c.q: A pilot flew 3, 5, 4, and 8 flights on four days. What is the mean number of flights?
m10c.how: Add: 3 + 5 + 4 + 8 = 20. Divide by the 4 days: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. (4.5 is the median.)

m10c.q: The data are 2, 3, 3, 4, and 28. Which measure of center best describes a typical value?
m10c.a: The median, because 28 is much larger than the rest
choices: The median, because 28 is much larger than the rest
The mean, because it uses every value
The mode, because 28 appears most often
The range, because the data are spread out
m10c.how: 28 is an outlier. It pulls the mean up to 8, which is bigger than almost every value. The median, 3, sits in the middle of the typical values.

m10c.q: The mean of 4 numbers is 7. What is the sum of the 4 numbers?
m10c.how: Mean = sum ÷ number of values, so sum = mean × number of values = 7 × 4 = 28.

m10c.q: Four test scores are 80, 90, 70, and x. The mean is 80. What is x?
m10c.how: The sum must be 80 × 4 = 320. The three known scores add to 80 + 90 + 70 = 240. So x = 320 − 240 = 80.

m10d.how: Range = greatest − least = 19 − 4 = 15. (10.4 is the mean.)

m10d.q: The data in order are 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11, 12, 14. The lower quartile is 4.5 and the upper quartile is 11.5. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
m10d.how: IQR = upper quartile − lower quartile = 11.5 − 4.5 = 7. (12 is the range.)

m10d.q: Two airlines both have a mean delay of 10 minutes. Airline A's delays have a range of 4 minutes, and Airline B's have a range of 30 minutes. Which airline's delays are more predictable?
m10d.a: Airline A, because its delays vary less
choices: Airline A, because its delays vary less
Airline B, because its range is bigger
They are the same, because the means are equal
m10d.how: The means match, but A's delays are packed close together (range 4), while B's are spread out (range 30). Less spread means more predictable.

m10d.q: Find the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of 2, 4, 6, and 8.
m10d.how: The mean is 20 ÷ 4 = 5. The distances from 5 are 3, 1, 1, and 3. Their mean is 8 ÷ 4 = 2. (5 is the mean and 6 is the range.)

m10d.q: The data are 5, 5, 5, and 5. What is the range?
m10d.how: Range = greatest − least = 5 − 5 = 0. Every value is the same, so there is no spread at all.

m10d.q: A box plot has a minimum of 10, a lower quartile of 15, a median of 20, an upper quartile of 30, and a maximum of 40. What is the range?
m10d.how: Range = maximum − minimum = 40 − 10 = 30. (15 is the IQR, 30 − 15.)

m10d.q: Use the same box plot: minimum 10, lower quartile 15, median 20, upper quartile 30, maximum 40. About what fraction of the data is between 15 and 30?
m10d.how: 15 and 30 are the lower and upper quartiles. The box between them holds the middle half of the data.

m10d.q: Set A is 9, 10, 11. Set B is 1, 10, 19. Which set has the greater spread?
choices: You cannot tell without the mean
m10d.how: Set A's range is 11 − 9 = 2. Set B's range is 19 − 1 = 18. Both have a mean of 10, but Set B is much more spread out.
